terminology.stair_carriage: stringer (US influence) or string (UK influence — both used)

terminology_notes: AU terminology sits between UK and US usage.
'Baluster' is more common than the UK 'spindle'.
Otherwise closer to UK vocabulary than US.

regulations.primary_reference: National Construction Code (NCC), Volume 1 (Building Code of Australia) for commercial, Volume 2 for residential. Referenced Australian Standard AS 1657 for stairs, ramps, ladders.

residential_ncc_volume_2.note_pitch: For domestic stairs; steeper for industrial/access ladders.
residential_ncc_volume_2.baluster_gap_rule: 125mm sphere may not pass through (looser than UK's 100mm rule)
residential_ncc_volume_2.note: AU 125mm rule is more relaxed than UK 100mm — but customer expectation and child safety still favour tighter spacing.

regulations.glass_balustrade: Grade A safety glass (toughened or laminated) per AS 1288. Height requirements per NCC — typically 1000mm above finished floor level on landings and balconies over 1000mm above the ground.
referenced_standards: AS 1657 — Fixed platforms, walkways, stairways and ladders
AS 1288 — Glass in buildings — Selection and installation
AS 1428 — Design for access and mobility

climate_considerations: Bushfire zones (BAL rating): timber species selection restricted in bushfire-prone areas. External and semi-external stairs may require BAL-rated timber or non-combustible substitutes.
Coastal (Queensland, WA): high humidity + salt air favours engineered timber and marine-grade finishes over solid.
Tropical north: monsoon humidity extremes — solid timber species selection critical to avoid seasonal movement.
Alpine (VIC, TAS): significant seasonal humidity swing.
External timber must be species-rated for outdoor use — hardwoods like Spotted Gum, Blackbutt, Ironbark preferred.
cultural_preferences: Modern glass-and-timber stairs are dominant in new-build metropolitan homes.
Outdoor timber stairs (deck stairs, external access) are much more common than in UK.
Australian hardwoods (Spotted Gum, Blackbutt, Tasmanian Oak, Jarrah, Blackwood) preferred over imported oak/walnut for character projects — supports local industry.
'Queenslander' traditional homes have external timber staircases as a signature feature.
Glass balustrades on external decks and stairs almost universal in coastal new builds.

tasmanian_oak.notes: Not related to European oak - commercial name for Eucalyptus regnans, obliqua, delegatensis. Light colour, straight grain, popular for interior stairs.

blackbutt.notes: Light-to-medium colour, durable, coastal-suitable, BAL-rated for bushfire areas.

spotted_gum.notes: Beautiful figured grain, very durable, common for external and premium interior stairs.

jarrah.notes: Rich red-brown WA hardwood, dense and durable, luxury choice.

blackwood.notes: Tasmanian species, walnut-like appearance, premium interior use.

ironbark.notes: Extremely dense and durable, favoured for structural and external stairs.

imported_oak.notes: American White Oak and European Oak imported — still popular but less patriotic than Australian species.

supplier_categories.trade_focus: Mitre 10, Home Timber & Hardware, Trade Tools

supplier_categories.stair_specialists: Signature Stairs, Barestairs, Stairbuilder, Aussie Stairs — bespoke manufacturers per state
supplier_categories.glass_balustrade: Glass and Metal, Balcony Systems, Frameless Impressions, TAG Balustrades
supplier_categories.note: AU supplier directory is not built in NEX yet — V2 target.

queenslander.notes: Traditional elevated timber house with external timber staircase as a signature feature. Timber species and durability critical.

californian_bungalow.notes: Common in Sydney, Melbourne inner suburbs. Modest internal stair; renovation-friendly.

modern_open_plan_metro.notes: Floating and open-riser stairs increasingly common. Glass balustrades dominant.

warehouse_conversion.notes: Melbourne + Sydney inner-city. Industrial style: steel + hardwood.

regulatory_warnings: Bushfire Attack Level (BAL) rating drives materials choice for external stairs in bushfire zones — do not spec unrated timber in BAL-12.5 or above.
State-specific building regulations layer on top of NCC — Victoria, NSW, Queensland, WA all have local variations.
Coastal humidity + salt air degrades finishes faster than temperate zones — spec marine-grade or plan for more frequent maintenance.
Historic Queenslander stairs may retain original non-compliant dimensions under heritage protection.
